<reflection>
The high-catalyst experiment has begun to discriminate:
- M8 and M6 (catalyst activation/ligand mechanisms) fit best (~-39).
- M7 (substrate-dependent complexation) fits better than the main group.
- M2 (catalyst dimerization) is slightly better than M1.
- M3, M4, M5 are poor.
- Most other mechanisms (M1, M9-M20) still cluster together.

The fact that M6/M8 (which involve catalyst activation - a slow "induction" to active form) fit better at high [cat] suggests there may be a lag or saturation behavior. However, many other mechanisms still compete. I need to probe product inhibition/deactivation and catalyst-substrate dependencies more.
</reflection>

<hypothesis>
To further discriminate, I should add product at the start. This will:
- Directly test M12 (P+cat inactivation) and M17 (P+catS inactivation) - they should show much slower kinetics with added product.
- Test reversibility (M1's k-2) - added product should slow the forward rate if reversible.
- Distinguish product-related inhibition from catalyst deactivation (M9, M11, M13, M14, M18, M19, M20) which should be unaffected by initial product.
- Distinguish from M6/M8 (catalyst activation) - should be unaffected by initial product.

Using moderate substrate (1.0 M), moderate catalyst (0.01 M, baseline), and significant initial product (0.3 M) will cleanly test product effects.
</hypothesis>
